title: The Narrow Hallway
premise: A neon-horror escape microgame where the player sprints down a narrow corridor toward an exit while a hostile watcher periodically locks on and punishes movement.
interaction_model: Single-input hold-to-move and release-to-stop control scheme, playable with pointer/touch hold on the canvas or spacebar hold on keyboard, plus start/restart UI buttons.
objective: Reach 100% exit progress without moving during the watcher's active attack phase.
progression: A single-run arcade loop: start from the menu, move during safe windows, freeze during warning/attack escalation, accumulate progress toward the exit, then either get caught for an immediate loss or reach the goal for victory.
theme: Sci-fi horror surveillance escape in a narrow hallway.
mood: Tense, claustrophobic, reactive, eerie, and arcade-styled with glitchy neon dread.
likely_audience: Players who enjoy short reaction-based arcade games
Players who like red-light-green-light tension loops
Mobile and desktop casual players seeking a quick reflex challenge
confidence_notes: High confidence in the basic gameplay loop because the entire game logic is visible in one HTML file.
High confidence that the main mechanic is timing-based freeze-or-move survival rather than free navigation.
Moderate confidence in genre labeling because the presentation resembles a runner while the rules behave more like a reaction survival game.
recreation_prompt: Create a compact browser arcade game called "The Narrow Hallway" set in a dark neon sci-fi corridor haunted by an unseen watcher. The player should control a tiny glowing courier-like spark moving along a single horizontal hallway progress line from left to right toward a bright exit marker. Use a one-button interaction model: hold touch, mouse, or spacebar to run forward, and release to freeze in place. Structure the game around a repeating threat cycle with three readable states: a safe idle phase, a short warning phase, and a dangerous lock-on attack phase. During safe phases the player can advance and fill an exit percentage meter from 0 to 100; during the attack phase any movement should instantly cause failure. Telegraph danger clearly with escalating HUD text, vignette color changes, glitch flashes, red surveillance-eye visuals, screen shake, and warning sound cues so the player learns to stop exactly on time. Present the experience with a dramatic start panel, a minimal HUD showing exit progress, and clear game-over and victory overlays. Add ambient horror audio, progress pings, win/fail stingers, subtle particles, floating creepy hallway words, scanlines, grain, and a polished neon-horror UI that feels readable on both desktop and mobile. The overall loop should be simple, tense, replayable, and built around surviving repeated freeze-or-run decisions until the player reaches the exit.
